01

Borrow the dream

As Claris, cross the stone bridge and touch NiGHTS in the Palace. Ground jump lets you greet eggs and evade the alarm.

02

Twenty little lights

Carry 20 blue chips into the Capture. Partial deposits count. Freeing the Ideya starts double-score bonus time.

03

Trace, don't just turn

Close a circle with your sparkling trail to Paraloop the things inside. C / X / ∞ traces a real circle; position its center carefully.

04

Know when to come home

Fly low into the Palace to bank, or pass above it for another scoring lap. After four Mares, drill Gillwing’s head—or loop his glowing tail.

The fine art of flight. Drill Dash turns wider and uses energy. Rings refill it. No direction input keeps your current heading. The pink Acrobat Rings turn shoulder tricks into points for 10 seconds. Miss the timer and you return to the meadow: rescue the Ideya on foot before the clock catches you.
Mystic Forest. Fly through the clear centre of spike rings. In Mare 4, the camera looks down on solid maze walls. Approach the red car, then move slowly to its green garage. Brake to let it catch up. Gulpo takes three charged hits. Enter a glowing propulsion unit, aim with the usual steering controls, then press Dash to launch. A normal Drill Dash does not damage Gulpo.

TWO DREAMS · RENDERING UPGRADE

About this dream.

Reverie in Bloom is an original fan adaptation of two Claris levels from NiGHTS into Dreams for Sega Saturn. Each level has four Mares, a boss, and results. This is not an emulated ROM or an official Sega product.

GENERATION DATESeptember 29, 2026
AI MODELGPT-6 Astra Pro
FORMATSingle offline HTML
Living Air · second graphics pass

Render the space between objects. The level now has height-weighted aerial haze, wind-driven mist banks, lit dust, source-local spray and a wake behind the player. The air has different behavior in each place. This is original environmental direction for this demo, not a claim about source-game content.

Spring Valley: warm clearing light, seed fluff and petals, moving spray at three waterfalls, shallow pools with surface highlights, reeds and grass. The fourth Mare has colder drifting flakes above the island.

Mystic Forest: denser low mist, cooler canopy light, pale spores, wind in hanging cloth, and small breath puffs while Claris is on foot. The maze has much less haze so its walls and route remain clear.

Boss spaces: Gillwing has low night haze and suspended dust. Gulpo has denser blue-green water haze and rising bubbles. The existing boss rules and attack timing are unchanged.

Interaction: a shared world-space wind field moves particles, canopy leaves, grass and hanging ribbons. Fast flight pushes nearby particles and forms a short swirling wake. A Paraloop draws the air inward. Mist opens around the flight wake and then fills it again. Cloth uses capped fixed-step Verlet chains with pinned roots. Pool rings respond to low passes.

Controls: Options → Air and weather: Clear, Natural, Rich. Natural is the default. Clear uses the earlier glow-and-particle atmosphere. Living scenery turns off the additional air and set dressing. Lens moisture and Environmental sound have separate switches. Source-local lens droplets stay at the screen edge and do not blur the flight route. Bloom remains optional and off by default.

Technical limits: aerial perspective is a height-weighted fragment fog calculation. Local mist and light shafts are depth-tested, procedurally shaded meshes. They are not full volumetric ray marching or shadowed volumetric lighting. There is no fluid solver or physically refractive wet lens. Water pools use PBR shading, not planar reflections. The atmospheric response does not change movement or collisions.

Resource limits: two additional shared soft-material batches handle fog and shafts. Dust and bubbles use instanced geometry. At most 208 ambient particle slots, 42 puffs, 24 wake samples, four air loops and twelve seven-node cloth chains exist. Balanced uses lower active counts. Auto still changes resolution and shadow cost from measured frame time. No additional rigid bodies, compute passes or external assets are required.

Audio additions: air-wind and air-water are original filtered-noise MP3 loops made for this update. They use the single embedded audio manifest and the existing audio unlock, mute and sound-effects volume. No source-game audio was added. The previous 29 manifest entries remain unchanged.

Hub migration: engine/wind.ts supplies the shared cosmetic wind field. game/air.ts owns the environmental state and submits geometry through DrawList. Engine renderer inputs use AirRenderState. TSL materials add vapor, shaft, dust and bubble masks. engine/presentation.ts draws the optional lens-edge layer with Canvas 2D. No GLSL, WGSL, ShaderMaterial or EffectComposer was added. The existing TypeScript archive packer and recovered r186 dependency provenance remain documented below.

Content checklist: both existing levels, all eight Mares, both bosses, the maze, car task, items, controls, score rules and local saves remain in scope. This pass adds environmental detail only. No new level, quest, upgrade or source narrative is claimed.

Generation: September 29, 2026 · GPT-6 Astra Pro.

Living Air · verification and known issues

September 29, 2026 · Chromium 144.0.7559.96 · Linux, software WebGL2. The current update passed 41 browser and environmental checks. A separate comparison passed 62 controlled gameplay-state checks against the supplied Dreamlight build.

Rendering: Three.js WebGPURenderer selected its automatic WebGL2 fallback. Natural, Rich, Clear, High and Balanced were exercised. The optional TSL bloom pipeline compiled and rendered. Both levels, the overhead maze, both boss spaces and the new water, mist and particle layers rendered without invalid instance values or uncaught application errors.

Environmental response: tests confirmed particle displacement from movement, Paraloop swirl, bounded cloth with pinned roots, local spray, drying after leaving the water, and particle expiry. Sustained Balanced spray stayed at or below 22 puffs. The full allocation remained within 208 mote slots, 42 puffs, 24 wakes, four air loops, eight ripple pulses and twelve seven-node cloth chains. These effects are cosmetic; no gameplay physics parameters changed.

Lens and input: a pixel check found moisture at the lens edge and none in the central flight view. Turning Lens moisture off cleared the overlay. Native keyboard input moved Claris. Trusted Chromium touch events held steering and Dash at the same time, moved NiGHTS through the normal fixed-step flight code, and produced an air wake. Releasing touch cleared both inputs. Portrait and landscape layouts were checked. The options panel was inspected after its opening animation and can scroll to every setting.

Gameplay regression: the 62 comparisons used identical fixed-step steering, dash, loop and trick inputs for both versions. They covered both openings, all eight Mares and both boss states. Pickup, deposit and bank checkpoints were also compared in controlled fixtures. Scores, movement, timers, item states, recovery-related state and boss state matched. These are regression fixtures, not a new uninterrupted human or input-only full-level playthrough. The previous full-level results remain below under their original build headings.

Audio and offline operation: all 31 MP3 entries decoded, including the two new environmental loops. No HTTP or HTTPS asset request occurred in the game tests. The executable archive has 18 embedded modules with SHA-256 checks. The three supplied r186 library modules and the level-data source remain unchanged. A final smoke test used the normal release HTML, not an always-enabled QA build.

Not verified: native WebGPU execution, physical controllers, physical phone or desktop frame rates, fullscreen and persistent saves across separate real file launches. Direct file navigation and a routed secure test origin were blocked by the managed browser policy. Testing supplied the complete file to an isolated browser document instead. No browser security policy was changed. Software-renderer frame times are not target-device performance measurements.

Known limits: local mist and shafts are layered, depth-tested TSL meshes, not full shadowed volumetric light or a fluid simulation. Intersections can be visible at close range. Water has no planar reflection and lens droplets do not refract the scene. Rich adds transparent overdraw; Natural is the default. The earlier custom archive-packer/Vite deviation, recovered r186 module provenance, and synthesized-audio deviation remain documented in this file. No new source-game recording is included.

Launch and controls

Open this HTML in a browser with WebGPU or WebGL2 enabled. Select Spring Valley or Mystic Forest. Select Enter the dream. No installation, network, local server, or build is needed. Audio starts after your first input. The Flight Guide covers keyboard, mouse, gamepad, and touch controls. Landscape gives the best view on a phone.

Each level has its own checkpoint and best score. A checkpoint is saved after each Mare. Options and Nightopian mood also save locally. When browser storage is blocked, these records last for the current session only.

Dreamlight visual update · September 29, 2026

Two dreams, now alive with light. Spring Valley and Mystic Forest retain their Mares, objectives, pickups, controls and bosses. This update changes presentation, not rules or scores.

Flight: pink and cyan wingtip trails, a fading Paraloop trace, a moving Drill Dash spiral, a small character glow, and speed lines at the screen edge. A short change in field of view adds speed feedback. No motion blur hides the flight path.

Pickups and action: soft blue-chip glows, gold star glints, sparks that move around rings, expanding pickup rings, enemy-hit bursts, a three-arm Paraloop vortex, glowing projectiles and fireworks at Mare and boss endings. Effects use world depth and do not cover the interface.

Living scenery: swaying tree crowns, drifting petals, fluttering butterflies, pulsing fireflies, moving waterfall streaks and spray, ground mist, and high aurora curtains. Forest shafts and mist are translucent geometry, not volumetric ray tracing. Rim light and a small local light improve character visibility.

Controls: Options → Visual effects has Subtle, Vivid and Spectacle. Vivid is the default. Living scenery can be switched off. Camera motion controls speed lines, the dash field-of-view effect and small impact movement. The browser's reduced-motion preference disables these camera effects. Bloom stays optional and is off by default. No full-screen light flashes were added.

Performance: effects use pooled, instanced geometry. The quality preset limits particle, trail and scenery density. There are at most 28 active action-effect groups and 72 wingtip history samples. Fixed-step timers control effect age. Auto still adjusts rendering resolution and shadow cost from measured frame time. Visual effects do not add physics bodies.

Engine: the new aura, glint, ribbon, mist and veil materials use MeshBasicNodeMaterial and TSL. The file still uses Three.js r186 WebGPURenderer, with WebGPU first and automatic WebGL2 fallback. There are no new runtime libraries or external assets. The existing source-audio and Vite substitutions remain unchanged.

Generation: 2026-09-29 · GPT-6 Astra Pro. The embedded TypeScript archive includes game/fx.ts and engine/presentation.ts. This is a visual enhancement of the two-level adaptation, not new source-game content.

Rendering and engine upgrade

The game now uses the real Three.js r186 WebGPURenderer. Startup awaits renderer.init(). WebGPU is primary. The renderer automatically selects WebGL2 when WebGPU is unavailable. Both backends use the same scene, meshes, node materials, lights, camera, and effects. The diagnostics show the active backend.

Rendering uses instanced vertex-colored geometry, MeshStandardNodeMaterial, per-instance TSL surface data, an original half-float HDR environment filtered by PMREM, hemisphere light, PCFShadowMap directional shadows, baked ground-contact shading and material ambient-occlusion factors, 4× MSAA, tone mapping, and optional TSL bloom through RenderPipeline. No custom GLSL, WGSL, ShaderMaterial, EffectComposer, or onBeforeCompile is used by the game.

Auto changes resolution and shadow resolution from measured frame time. High and Balanced use different pixel scales, shadow maps, bloom resolution, and particle limits. Bloom is off by default. The game uses fixed 60 Hz kinematic movement with interpolated rendering. It has no dynamic rigid bodies; Rapier is not needed.

Dependency provenance: The embedded r186 modules were recovered from an existing offline Library build after public package downloads failed. All recovered payload SHA-256 checks passed. The installed source exports REVISION 186, WebGPURenderer, Timer and RenderPipeline. The manifest pins three to 0.186.0. The recovered build's byte identity with the npm tarball was not independently verified. The file contains the MIT license.

Build-tool deviation: Vite could not be installed in this session. A deterministic local TypeScript transpile-and-archive step produced this file. This affects authoring only; no build tool runs in the browser.

Spring Valley source checklist
Source beat / contentWhere it works here
Claris, Courage, NiGHTS and the Ideya PalaceA brief four-light theft, walkable meadow, bridge chips, eggs, ground jump and dualization at the blue pavilion.
Mare 1: open meadow, upper chip/star cluster, descending pickups, Shleep, Capture, returning ring chain“The waking meadow.” A compact teaching circuit with the same pickup–Capture–Palace sequence.
Mare 2: low chips, rising rings, chip box, dash power, hidden power, tree-lined return“Through the green cathedral.” Longer vertical route; box holds eight chips; Paraloop reveals the hidden refill.
Mare 3: ring sequence, Shleep, Hollow, box, dash pickup, two Acrobat Rings“A ribbon in the wind.” Seed-firing Hollow, 10-second acrobat windows and a high Capture approach.
Mare 4: rising ring chain, mountain wind, summit stars, descending chips, Kircle“The snow-crowned sky.” A snow peak and real lift corridor, then a low green return.
Four 120-second Mares and four stolen IdeyasEach flight phase has its own timer, Capture and return; every completed Mare unlocks the next.
Twenty-chip Capture, partial deposits, speed bonus, double-score lapsCollide with the Capture to deposit. Release grants a remaining-time bonus. Bank low at the Palace, or pass high to continue.
Drill Dash, limited energy, ring refills, trick turns, ParaloopsFull directional steering; drill has a wider turning radius. Paraloops detect a closed polygon in the actual flight trail.
Links, stars, bonus ball, helper, hidden power, eight-chip boxPickup chains, a Mare 1 bonus challenge and hidden helper, Mare 2 refill, Mare 2/3 boxes and collectible stars.
Shleep grab / throw, Hollow seeds, Kircle contactDistinct encounters; drill and Paraloop defeat enemies. Throwing a Shleep creates a moving projectile.
Nightopians, eggs, Mepians and mood-influenced musicLocal friendly population, eggs hatch on foot, thrown-enemy contact creates a hybrid egg, mood changes the mix. Simplified, not the full Saturn A-Life simulation.
Timeout, scattered chips, alarm pursuit, waking failureDedualization discards the Mare score. The rescue continues on foot, with a pursuing alarm that can be jump-stunned.
Gillwing’s 21 segments, head drill, tail Paraloop, timed multiplierComplete boss arena after Mare 4. Repeated head strikes or one accurate tail loop reach the ending.
Mare grading, final score and replayPer-Mare results, time multiplier, technique bonus, A–F grade, best link, stars, Paraloops and local personal best.
Mystic Forest source checklist → demo
Source contentPlayable location
Claris's second dream; NiGHTS; four stolen IdeyasChoose Mystic Forest. The forest opening leads from Claris to the Palace. Four separately timed Mares each have a Capture and Palace return.
Forest setting and ruinsAll four routes use a distinct moonlit forest, taller trees, broken arches, mushrooms, stars, and cool lighting.
Chips, rings, boxes, chains and bonus lapsAll four Mares have more than 20 blue chips, their own routes, partial Capture deposits, link scoring, double-score laps and banking.
Spike ringsMares 1–4. A clear central crossing grants points and energy. The spiked rim costs five seconds.
Trick-ring passagesMare 3, Ribbons in starlight. Two ten-second trick windows use the existing full acrobatics system.
Overhead maze in Mare 4The winding star maze. The camera looks down on a horizontal flight plane. Solid walls, open passages and a maze minimap work during normal flight and bonus laps.
Red car and green garageMare 4. Approach the car to make it follow. Guide it around walls and brake to let it catch up. Parking it at the garage grants 5,000 points and a fanfare.
Gulpo and propulsion unitsAfter all four Mares, enter the underwater nightmare. Four units capture NiGHTS for aiming. Press Dash to launch. Three charged hits defeat Gulpo. Normal dashes do not damage him.
Boss timer, failure, retry, multiplier and endingGulpo has a 120-second timer, projectiles, hit feedback, checkpoint retry, a time multiplier, victory transition, final rank and saved best score.
Defining shared systemsManual and assisted Paraloops, Drill Dash, brake, energy, hidden items, bonus challenges, enemies, throws, Nightopians, eggs, Mepians, timeout recovery on foot, and the alarm clock remain available.
Adaptation choices and additions

All meshes, route coordinates, enemy placement, colors, and interface art are newly authored. These are guide-based adaptations, not exact Saturn maps. The forest Mare names, complete horizontal Mare 4 flight plane, maze wall layout, car-follow radius, 5,000-point garage reward, four propulsion-unit arrangement, aiming guide, charged-launch duration, and Gulpo projectile pattern are authored choices. The source-backed car task, overhead maze, spike rings, trick sections and propulsion-based three-hit boss remain distinct, working systems.

A level picker, separate records, a Next Dream result button, explicit boss aiming guide, maze minimap, optional steering assistance, and measured Auto quality are added for this demo.

Outside this two-level slice

All other dreams, Elliot's campaign, final bosses, Christmas content, Saturn multiplayer, full A-Life ecosystem simulation, exact original scoring tables, original map meshes and original source audio recordings are not included. No inactive menu option claims to offer these systems.

Previous build: verification and known issues

September 29, 2026 · Chromium 144.0.7559.96 · Linux. Forty-eight automated checks passed: 25 full-level progression checks and 23 interface, input, settings, audio and offline checks.

Complete Spring Valley run: normal movement inputs crossed the opening bridge, joined NiGHTS, collected and deposited chips in all four Mares, banked each Ideya, and defeated Gillwing with a closed tail Paraloop. The results screen showed 135,338 points, rank A.

Complete Mystic Forest run: normal movement inputs completed the opening and all four Mares, guided the red car into its garage, and defeated Gulpo with three propulsion strikes. The results screen showed 170,018 points, rank A.

These two runs advanced the unchanged 60 Hz game simulation with scripted stick, dash, brake and trick inputs. They did not teleport the player or force objective completion. Rendering was not run for every simulated frame. These are progression regressions, not human playthroughs or device frame-rate tests.

Renderer checks: the actual Three.js WebGPURenderer selected its WebGL2 fallback. Both quality presets and the optional TSL bloom pipeline rendered without application errors. Desktop, portrait and landscape layouts were rendered and inspected. Auto reduced resolution and shadow cost when the test supplied slow frame intervals.

Input and interface checks: keyboard movement, chorded mouse steering and dash, simulated gamepad input, pause on gamepad disconnect, simultaneous browser touch stick and dash, touch release, level selection, options, native range-key input, mute, pause/resume, Gulpo failure/retry and separate level checkpoints passed. All 29 embedded audio entries decoded. No HTTP or HTTPS request occurred during these checks.

Test limits: the managed browser blocked file:// navigation. The tests supplied the HTML to an isolated browser document and ran the same embedded module bootstrap. No browser security policy was changed. Native WebGPU was not available in that test origin. A real double-click launch, WebGPU execution, persistent storage across browser launches, native fullscreen, physical controllers and target-hardware frame rates remain unverified. Session-only saving worked when storage was blocked.

The renderer's full npm byte identity, physical-controller behavior, native fullscreen, and sustained performance on Samsung Galaxy S24 or RTX 3060 hardware are not certified. Local HTML launch and storage support depend on the browser. There is no screen-space ambient-occlusion pass; shadowing and material/contact shading provide depth.

Hub migration notes

Dreamlight integration: Preserve the new DrawList modes aura, glint, ribbon, mist and veil. They keep the existing 24-float instance layout. engine/renderer.ts owns their TSL definitions and pooled geometry. game/fx.ts submits only draw commands and reads game state. engine/presentation.ts draws the speed-line overlay with Canvas 2D. The renderer visual state carries only player position, energy and impact level. No compute shaders, custom GLSL/WGSL, or new physics system was added.

The engine folder owns Three.js startup, fallback, DrawList conversion, scene lighting, settings, diagnostics, audio, input and local storage. Game files use the engine's DrawList, camera, input, audio and storage interfaces. Replace this engine adapter with the hub adapter; keep the two level data sets and game logic unchanged.

Library imports in authored code use only three/webgpu and three/tsl. The bundled BloomNode imports the same bare names. No copied engine library is imported by path. The single-file archive uses Blob module URLs only after unpacking the embedded dependency bytes. A hub build should resolve the original bare imports normally and omit this offline archive bootstrap.

The custom DrawList's 24-float instance record, measured Auto-quality policy, kinematic collision checks, route-to-world mapping and generated audio manifest are the integration points to preserve. There are no custom WebGL shaders or WebGPU-only visual features. Replace the local TypeScript archive build with the hub's Vite tooling.
